correctness.rationale: Subtracting the two binomial coefficients gives (i−j)(i+j−1)!/(i!j!) in degree i+j≤n. Both factorials and nonzero index differences involved are units. Thus for unequal leading degrees r,s with r+s≤n the first possible coefficient is nonzero. For 2r≤n a commuting y has order at least r; subtracting a multiple of x eliminates degree r and leaves exactly the free tail at degrees >n−r. For 2r>n only that tail is possible. This proves both dimension formulas, including r=n. For a tuple of minimum order r≤floor(n/2), the nonzero degree-r row determines the common direction of all rows through n−r; the r upper rows are free. For larger minimum order all products between tuple elements vanish, so the count is the difference of two free tail counts. Adding the zero tuple gives N, with k=1 giving q^n. The centralizer sum gives the pair specialization; the largest base is q^(h+1), with one leading summand of weight 1 for n=2h and two of weights q and 1 for n=2h+1. Independent bounded enumeration of the original binomial multiplication at (q,n)=(5,3) gave 3625 commuting pairs and 93125 commuting triples; this is corroboration only. The supplied script was inspected but not executed.

evidence: The indexed derivation census, Proof §1, describes the full centralizer as D_(u h) for f=t^v u with h supported on indices j satisfying j+v−1≥N or j≡v mod p; it covers all N and all finite fields. The other references study a zero-product maximal abelian ideal over C, or general Zinbiel commutator identities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Here all j,v are less than p, so j≡v means j=v, and the remaining subspace is exactly the high-degree tail, invariant under multiplication by the unit u. Lift to the Zinbiel space with the free e_n to recover the claimed centralizer subspace, not just its dimension. The complex ideal and the Tortkara identities do not count the claimed tuples.

originality.rationale: The strongest distinct indexed result supplies the exact centralizer subspaces of all truncated polynomial derivations, not just related numbers. Under the factorial coordinate map the Zinbiel commutation relation is exactly the pullback of that derivation commutation relation, with one free dimension. The advertised subspaces, pair census and higher-arity strata follow directly, and the parity asymptotic is a leading-term readout of those strata. This establishes equivalent coverage and a direct implication; same-day indexing does not resolve priority.
